_note: Segment-driven model (as ETERNAL/SWIGGY): marketplace NMV grows; revenue and adjusted EBITDA are % of NMV. New initiatives (financial services, low-cost local logistics, AI services, Kirana Club from Q2FY27) on revenue with a capped loss. Reported EBITDA = segment adjusted EBITDA − ESOP. Valued on sum of the parts on Sep-28E (roll FY28E/FY29E 50:50). ₹ crore.

segments.name: Marketplace (incl. Valmo logistics, ads, Meesho Mall)
segments._why: NMV +38.6% in FY26 and +34% in Q1FY27 (orders +29%, fewer cancellations and returns). Management guides to ~25% NMV CAGR for five years, higher in the early years (Q1FY27 call). The big sale moves from Q2 to Q3 this year, so Q2FY27 growth will look soft and Q3 strong. We use 30% / 26% / 23% (26% a year FY26-29E), between Jefferies (25%) and Citi (27%).
segments._revWhy: Marketplace revenue (seller fees for logistics, ads, platform fees) was 30.4% of NMV in FY26 and 31.9% in Q1FY27 (Q1FY26 ~28.8%) as cancellations and returns fell and ads grew. We assume 31.8-32.2%.
segments._marginWhy: Marketplace adjusted EBITDA was −2.8% of NMV in FY26 (Valmo scale-up costs in Q2-Q3) and −1.2% in Q1FY27, with contribution margin back to 4.6%. Growth spends step up in Q2-Q3FY27 (festive), so FY27E is −1.5%. Break-even in FY28E (+0.2%) and +1.3% in FY29E as ads and operating leverage lift contribution margin ~0.5pp a year and fixed costs fall as a share of NMV. Below Citi (2.1% by FY29E); Jefferies has 3% only by FY30.

segments.name: New initiatives (financial services, local logistics, AI services, Kirana Club)
segments._why: Revenue ₹12 cr in FY26 (₹4 cr in FY25). Kirana Club (B2B marketplace for small retailers) joins from Q2FY27. We assume ₹50 / 100 / 170 cr; revenue is immaterial to value.
segments._marginWhy: Loss ₹70 cr in FY26 and ₹39 cr in Q1FY27. Management caps new-initiative losses at ~₹200 cr a year (Q1FY27 call); with Kirana Club added we assume ₹180 cr in FY27E and the full ₹200 cr cap in FY28-29E.

_unallocWhy: Unallocated items were +₹1.9 cr in FY26 and nil in Q1FY27.
_esopWhy: Share-based pay ₹182 cr in FY26 (₹320 cr in FY25, when the promoters' options vested early) and ₹40 cr in Q1FY27 (₹160 cr annualised), rising with post-IPO grants. Non-cash, but it dilutes shareholders.
_capexWhy: Capex ₹121 cr in FY26 (incl. payables for capital goods), up from ₹23-35 cr in FY24-25 as servers, sort-centre equipment and offices were added. An asset-light marketplace: Valmo's partners own the trucks and sort centres.
_depWhy: Depreciation ₹47 cr in FY26 on ₹320 cr of gross block; ₹20 cr in Q1FY27 (₹80 cr annualised). 20% of average gross block gives ~₹80-120 cr for FY27-29E.
_treasuryWhy: Other income ₹416 cr in FY26 and ₹447 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (company reconciliation) on a cash balance of ₹6,500-6,750 cr: ~6.5%.
_interestLabel: Finance cost (lease interest and interest on MSME dues)
_interestWhy: Finance cost ₹9 cr in FY26, ₹2 cr in Q1FY27. No borrowings besides ₹63 cr of leases.
_taxWhy: Statutory 25.2%. Tax applies only to positive profit in the model. Meesho has carried-forward losses on which no deferred tax asset is booked (AR FY26 tax note), which could shelter the first profits; we do not count that (conservative).

otherTreasury.label: Bank deposits held in other assets (treasury)
otherTreasury._why: Company cash balance ₹6,750 cr at Mar-26 (FY26 annual report) less ₹3,103 cr shown as cash and investments on Screener's balance sheet; the difference is bank deposits reported in other financial assets.

dcf._betaWhy: Long-duration, loss-making consumer internet stock; 1.1 gives a 13.1% cost of equity, as for Eternal. No debt, so cost of equity = WACC.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~23% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 12% reported EBITDA margin on revenue ≈ 3.9% of NMV at 32% revenue/NMV.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~1% of revenue at maturity (FY26 1.0%): servers and sort-centre equipment.

parts.name: Marketplace
parts.note: EV/NMV, the yardstick Jefferies uses (1.6x Jun-28E NMV at initiation) and the only one we can derive from the stock's own history while it makes losses. Own EV / one-year-forward NMV since 1-Jan-2026 (listing month Dec-2025 skipped as IPO premium): median 1.23x; the internet peers with a usable P/E (Info Edge, IndiaMART) moved −2.7% against their own medians over the same window: 1.23x × 0.973 = 1.20x. Bull 1.25x (own median, no sector move); bear 1.10x (own 25th percentile × the move). Applied to Sep-28E NMV.

parts.name: New initiatives
parts.metricLabel: FY28E adjusted EBITDA (loss) × PV factor of losses to breakeven
parts.note: Start-up losses valued as the present value of losses still to come: ~₹200 cr a year (the budget cap) for four more years at 13.1% (annuity factor 3.0); bull two years (1.7), bear six years (4.0). Any value of a business that does succeed is upside.

parts.name: Kirana Club purchase price
parts.metricLabel: Cash consideration, paid in three tranches by Mar-27
parts.note: Board approved on 12-Jun-2026: ~₹202 cr in cash for 100% of Kirana Club (B2B marketplace for small retailers), paid in three tranches to complete by 31-Mar-2027. Not yet in the model's Mar-27 cash; its losses sit inside new initiatives.

parts.name: Contested income-tax demands
parts.metricLabel: Bear case only: demands paid in full
parts.note: Income-tax demands of ₹1,500 cr (AY2023-24) and ₹572 cr (AY2022-23, stayed by the Karnataka High Court) are contested and not provided for (AR FY26 note 29). Base and bull: nil (company has appealed); bear: paid in full.

parts.name: Net cash at end-FY27E
parts.note: Model forecast: cash, bank deposits and treasury investments less lease liabilities at Mar-27.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: Two parts at different stages: a marketplace near break-even, valued on order value (EV/NMV) because EBITDA is still negative, and capped start-up losses valued as the present value of losses to come; plus cash. Primary.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Whole-company cash flows over 15 years at a 13.1% cost of equity (Ventura, BofA and JM Financial use a DCF); tests whether the order-value multiple is backed by a credible path to cash.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA (street multiple)
methods.why: The street's most common disclosed method: EV/EBITDA on FY29E (Citi 50x, JM Financial ~45x implied, BofA 30x; median 45x). On our FY29E EBITDA (after ESOP) it shows how much of the street's value rests on margins we do not yet forecast.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: NMV grows ~30% a year to FY29E (34/30/27%) and marketplace margin reaches 2.1% of NMV by FY29E (Citi's path) as ads scale; the market keeps its own median 1.25x forward NMV; new-initiative losses stop after two years.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Amazon Bazaar, Flipkart Shopsy and quick commerce slow NMV growth to ~19% a year and margins stall near break-even (0.3% of NMV in FY29E); 1.10x NMV (own 25th percentile); new initiatives burn ₹200 cr a year for six years; the contested ₹2,072 cr of tax demands are paid.
